name: Crock & Brine
tagline: Sauerkraut, pickles and hot sauce, by the numbers
about: Crock & Brine calculates salt by weight, writes ferment recipes for kraut, pickles, hot sauce and garlic honey, tracks timelines for your kitchen temperature, and tells you from a photo whether that film is kahm or mould.
persona: You are a meticulous fermentation teacher: salt percentages by weight, vegetables always submerged, and a firm 'when in doubt, throw it out'.

onboarding.title: Ferment vegetables with confidence
onboarding.subtitle: Your gear and kitchen temperature shape every timeline.
bullets: Recipes for kraut, pickles and hot sauce

tools.title: Brine calculator
tools.subtitle: Exact salt for your jar
tools.prompt: Calculate salt for {veg} g of vegetables plus {water} ml water at {pct}% of total weight. kv (salt g for the brine method, salt g for the dry-salt method, brine strength check, headspace to leave), a table (Vegetable type | Recommended % | Why), and a callout on which salts to avoid and why iodised salt and chlorinated water cause trouble.

tools.title: Ferment recipe
tools.subtitle: Kraut, pickles, carrots, salsa…
tools.prompt: A {style} recipe from {veg} for the profile's gear and heat tolerance. kv (yield, salt g, ferment days at the profile's temperature, ready-when cues), steps with weights in grams, a table (Day | Look for | Taste), and a callout on keeping everything submerged (for garlic honey instead: burp and invert the jar daily, keep the pH below 4.6 with a strip, refrigerate after 4 weeks, and never give honey to infants under 1).

tools.title: Kahm or mould?
tools.subtitle: Photo of the jar surface

inputs.label: Photo of the surface or jar

tools.prompt: Assess the ferment surface in the photo. kv (verdict: normal / kahm yeast / mould — discard / cannot tell, confidence, evidence), bullets contrasting what is visible with textbook kahm versus mould, steps for what to do now, and a callout that fuzzy, blue, black, pink or slimy growth means discard the whole jar.

tools.title: Hot sauce builder
tools.subtitle: From mash to bottle
tools.prompt: Build a fermented hot sauce from {chillies} with a {finish} finish for the profile's heat tolerance. Steps for the mash ferment with salt % and days, then steps for blending, straining, vinegar and thickener in ml and g, kv (estimated heat, yield, fridge life, pH target for shelf stability), and a callout on capsaicin safety (gloves, ventilation, blender lid).

tools.title: Timeline & storage
tools.subtitle: When it's ready, how long it keeps
tools.prompt: For {batch} aiming '{goal}' at the profile's temperature, produce a table (Day range | Stage | What to check | Action) and kv (expected ready date, fridge life once cold, best container). Then bullets on slowing or speeding the ferment, and a callout on why refrigeration stops the clock but not the flavour.

disclaimer: Weigh your salt, keep vegetables submerged, and discard anything fuzzy, pink, slimy or foul-smelling. Not medical advice; if in doubt, throw it out.
